html:
The Semipalatinsk Test Site on the steppe of northeast Kazakhstan was the main Soviet nuclear weapons testing ground. From 1949 to 1989 the Soviet Union set off 456 nuclear tests there, more than a hundred of them in the open air.

It began with the RDS-1 test of 1949. The area was called empty, but villages lay close by and people were rarely moved or warned. Fallout drifted over farms and towns around Semipalatinsk. Hundreds of thousands of people were exposed to radiation over the years, and doctors have recorded high rates of cancer and birth defects.

Testing went underground in the 1960s. In 1989 the Kazakh poet Olzhas Suleimenov founded the Nevada Semipalatinsk movement, one of the first mass protest movements in the Soviet Union, and the last test took place that year. Nursultan Nazarbayev closed the site in 1991. Kazakhstan's own memory of the tests shaped its choice to give up nuclear weapons.
sum: The Semipalatinsk Test Site on the steppe of northeast Kazakhstan was the main Soviet nuclear weapons testing ground. From 1949 to 1989 the Soviet Union set off 456 nuclear tests there, more than a hundred of them in the open air.
